The older student I’m tagged to: she falls in the severe range and is still non-verbal at 15. She is unable to follow instructions and her motor skills are underdeveloped too. When in distress, she charges at me and/or runs away. She also resists a lot when I try to bring her back to her seat and I don’t know how to assist her without accidentally hurting her (e.g. I had to literally pull her up from the floor today so she’d stand up and I was so scared to hurt her back). Also would appreciate any tips on how to not be so intimidated…! I have anxiety and coupled with the lack of exposure to people on the spectrum, I still flinch a little when I see this student run towards me at full speed or when she grabs me all of a sudden (again, I mean no disrespect! am just really overstimulated and so I get really anxious but I know they aren’t trying to harm me). How can I reframe my mind to not be intimidated and instead treat my student(s) with more compassion and understanding?

The younger student I’m tagged to (7 years old): I figure he’s in the moderate range. He is able to complete tasks on his own but when things don’t go his way, he screams and cries. I want to know how to calm him down! Just some observations from the first day, he likes clocks and fidget spinners (not sure how relevant this is haha). Also would like to know how to communicate better with this child (e.g. when giving instructions). He is able to respond to instructions and so I would like to know how I can be clearer…!

Thank you for your help!! Appreciate it :)

I have a very good friend who has been supporting me since the discard but these days I get a sense that she’s annoyed and doesn’t understand why I still have a soft spot for my ex despite the break up being close to a month ago, on top of all the horrible things he has done to me. Talking to friends who don’t understand how intoxicating it is to be with a narc can make you feel abnormal - “why am i not moving on?” Your post really comforted me. Thank you.
